title: Microsoft Teams: separate attendance and engagement report policy for Teams events
summary: The rollout dates, policy values, administrator paths and commands are supported by Microsoft's notice and documentation. Two minor corrections remain: the licensing model understates the published Teams events entitlement, and the checklist's policy-assignment check has no matching control-table entry.

claims.claim: Microsoft plans a separate attendance and engagement report policy for Teams events.
claims.quote: Teams events will soon have a separate attendance and engagement report policy from the "CsTeamsMeetingPolicy" attendance and engagement report policy.

The new control is admin-opt-in: its default does not restrict organisers' report access until an administrator configures a restriction.
claims.quote: On, organizers can turn it off (default)- Organizers can view and download attendance and engagement reports for events and can disable attendance and engagement reporting in event options.

claims.claim: Licensing is unknown because no separate entitlement for the new policy setting is published.
claims.quote: All eligible Teams licenses include the foundational capabilities needed to create and run events, engage attendees, review attendance reports, and publish event recordings.
claims.fix: Set licensing.model to "included". Retain the existing licence-category explanation and add: "The setting is an option inside licensed Teams events; Microsoft has not published a separate licence or meter specific to this policy setting." The product entitlement is documented at https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoftteams/events-licensing.

claims.where: controls[0].api; Governance controls; Governance guidance: At rollout
claims.claim: Set-CsTeamsEventsPolicy -Identity <policy name> -AllowEngagementReport ForceDisabled blocks events attendance and engagement reports.
claims.quote: -Identity: Unique identifier assigned to the Teams Events policy. ForceDisabled: Off. Organizers cannot view or download attendance and engagement reports.

claims.where: controls[0].scope; Risk assessment: Security & identity; Scope
claims.claim: The events policy is user-level and controls report access for the organiser assigned that policy.
claims.quote: User-level policy for tenant admin to configure options for customizing Teams events experiences. Use this cmdlet to update an existing policy.

claims.claim: The Set-CsTeamsEventsPolicy reference marks the events policy as still in preview.
claims.quote: This cmdlet allows you to configure options for customizing Teams events experiences. Note that this policy is currently still in preview.

claims.claim: The events parameter value Enabled means On, with organisers able to turn it off.
claims.quote: Enabled: On, but organizers can turn it off.

claims.claim: The events parameter value Disabled means Off, with organisers able to turn it on.
claims.quote: Disabled: Off, but organizers can turn it on.

claims.claim: The events parameter value ForceEnabled means On and cannot be turned off by organisers.
claims.quote: ForceEnabled: On. Organizers cannot turn off attendance and engagement reports.

claims.claim: The events parameter value ForceDisabled means Off with no organiser view or download.
claims.quote: ForceDisabled: Off. Organizers cannot view or download attendance and engagement reports.

claims.claim: Teams admin center > Meetings > Events policies > policy > Edit reaches events policy editing.
claims.quote: In the left navigation of the Microsoft Teams admin center, go to Meetings > Meeting policies or Events policies. Choose the policy by clicking to the left of the policy name, and then select Edit.

claims.claim: Grant-CsTeamsEventsPolicy -Identity <user> -Policy <policy name> assigns an events policy to that user.
claims.quote: Grant-CsTeamsEventsPolicy -Identity "user1@contoso.com" -Policy DisablePublicWebinars

claims.claim: The Grant-CsTeamsEventsPolicy reference also marks the policy as preview.
claims.quote: Assigns Teams Events policy to a user, group of users, or the entire tenant. Note that this policy is currently still in preview.
